title: Explicit worktree identities and destructive scope over the real socket

cases.summary: In an isolated Git fixture, worktree.create from the primary checkout's explicit id returns branch, source and seq; worktree.open links one workspace; worktree.remove without group scope is scope_required and names the checkout and workspace; with group scope it closes exactly that workspace and removes the checkout; worktree.list then shows only the primary checkout.

worktree.remove of a dirty checkout with scope {group:false, force:false} is checkout_dirty, error.data.affected lists the checkout id, and the untracked file and every workspace survive. The plan's flat {checkout_id, force, group} payload without op_id is invalid_params before any effect.
